content.text:
**Short answer:** Gold does **not look obviously undervalued** right now. It looks more like a **high-priced “fair-to-expensive” asset with strong structural support**. It *could still rise* if real rates fall, the dollar weakens, geopolitical risk stays high, or central banks keep buying—but the easy “cheap gold” argument is weaker after the big rally.

As of **June 8, 2026**, SPDR Gold Shares (**GLD**) is trading around **$396.45**, reflecting gold prices that are already near historically high levels. 

### Why gold might still be undervalued

Gold bulls have a credible case:

- **Central banks are still buying heavily.** The World Gold Council reported estimated **net central-bank purchases of 244 tonnes in Q1 2026**, continuing the elevated buying trend that has been in place since 2022. ([gold.org](https://www.gold.org/goldhub/research/gold-demand-trends/gold-demand-trends-q1-2026/central-banks?utm_source=openai))
- **ETF and investment demand remain supportive.** Gold-backed ETF holdings rose in Q1 2026, though at a slower pace than in the very strong 2025 period. ([gold.org](https://www.gold.org/download/file/20774/GDT-Q1-2026-Exec-Summary.pdf?utm_source=openai))
- **Macro uncertainty supports gold.** The World Gold Council’s 2026 outlook points to economic uncertainty, central-bank demand, ETF flows, and geopolitical tension as major drivers for gold. ([gold.org](https://www.gold.org/goldhub/research/gold-outlook-2026?utm_source=openai))
- **If real interest rates fall**, gold usually benefits because the opportunity cost of holding a non-yielding asset declines. UBS also recently argued that lower real rates and continued central-bank demand could support gold. ([ubs.com](https://www.ubs.com/global/en/wealthmanagement/insights/chief-investment-office/house-view/2026/weekly-key-messages/_jcr_content/root/contentarea/mainpar/toplevelgrid_1825995/col_2/textimage_copy.0893710422.file/dGV4dD0vY29udGVudC9kYW0vYXNzZXRzL3dtL2dsb2JhbC9jaW8vaG91c2Utdmlldy9kb2N1bWVudC9nb2xkLWVuLTE2NTkwOTcucGRm/gold-en-1659097.pdf?utm_source=openai))

### Why gold may not be undervalued

The bearish or cautious case is also strong:

- **Gold has already had a huge run.** In 2025, gold surged to record highs, driven by ETF inflows, central-bank buying, a softer dollar, and safe-haven demand. ([kiplinger.com](https://www.kiplinger.com/investing/gold/should-you-buy-gold-what-the-experts-say?utm_source=openai))
- **Much of the bullish story may already be priced in.** Central-bank buying, geopolitical risk, de-dollarization, and expected rate cuts are no longer hidden themes.
- **Gold produces no cash flow.** Unlike stocks, bonds, or real estate, gold has no earnings, coupon, dividend, or rent stream. That makes “undervalued” harder to prove.
- **If real yields stay high or the dollar strengthens**, gold could stagnate or fall even if the long-term strategic case remains intact.

### My view

I’d frame it this way:

| Time horizon | Is gold undervalued? | Why |
|---|---:|---|
| **Short term** | **Probably not clearly undervalued** | Price already reflects a lot of bullish news. |
| **Medium term** | **Possibly fairly valued with upside optionality** | Depends on Fed cuts, dollar weakness, ETF flows, and central-bank demand. |
| **Long term** | **Reasonable as a hedge, not a screaming bargain** | Useful against currency debasement, geopolitical risk, and portfolio shocks. |

### Practical takeaway

If you own **no gold**, a modest allocation—say **3–10% of a diversified portfolio**, depending on risk tolerance—can make sense as insurance. But I would be cautious about treating gold as a deeply undervalued asset after such a strong rally.

So: **gold may still be strategically attractive, but I would not call it obviously undervalued today.**
